boards.school_name: State University of New York at New Paltz
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-purchase ways to spend time on campus and around New Paltz, with student-access details where relevant.

cards.title: Browse the Dorsky galleries
cards.subtitle: Smiley Art Building, SUNY New Paltz
cards.notes: Walk through the galleries and use the museum’s digital guide to discuss works together. Follow gallery rules: no food or drink and no flash photography.
cards.short_summary: A campus art visit with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY New Paltz states that admission to the Dorsky Museum is free.
cards.source_title: Saturday Arts Lab Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Museum hours are listed by SUNY New Paltz; check before going.

cards.title: Catch a planetarium show
cards.subtitle: SUNY New Paltz campus
cards.notes: Check the planetarium’s show listing, then meet for a sky simulation featuring stars, planets, constellations, and deep-sky objects.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY New Paltz lists the John R. Kirk Planetarium as free for SUNY New Paltz students.
cards.access_notes: Free for SUNY New Paltz students; confirm the current show schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Walk Historic Huguenot Street
cards.subtitle: Historic Huguenot Street, New Paltz
cards.notes: Take the paved street past the stone houses, burial ground, church, and Munsee wigwam. Keep this to the free self-guided outdoor walk.
cards.short_summary: Explore the historic street without taking a paid tour.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY New Paltz says visitors can walk through Historic Huguenot Street for free on their own.
cards.access_notes: Guided tours are separate; use the public street for the no-cost option.

cards.entity_name: SUNY New Paltz Campus Tree Walk
cards.title: Follow the Campus Tree Walk
cards.subtitle: SUNY New Paltz campus
cards.notes: Use the tree-walk guide to choose a route, identify trees, and pause at the numbered specimens with friends between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY New Paltz identifies a Campus Tree Walk for learning what grows on campus.
cards.access_notes: Self-guided outdoor activity on campus; use the university’s tree-walk resource.

cards.title: Ride the New Paltz Loop
cards.subtitle: Campus and New Paltz
cards.notes: Bring your student ID and use the daily loop to connect campus with town, then plan a no-purchase walk at your stop.
cards.short_summary: A student-ID ride between campus and town.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY New Paltz says the New Paltz Loop travels through campus and New Paltz daily and is free with student ID.
cards.access_notes: Free with SUNY New Paltz student ID; consult the posted schedule.

cards.title: Take the Ulster–Poughkeepsie Link
cards.subtitle: New Paltz to Poughkeepsie train station
cards.notes: Use your student ID for the no-cost ride to the Poughkeepsie train station, then keep plans local unless you choose to buy onward travel.
cards.short_summary: A free student-ID regional transit connection.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY New Paltz states that the Ulster-Poughkeepsie Link is free with student ID.
cards.access_notes: Free with SUNY New Paltz student ID; verify the current route schedule.

cards.title: Walk or roll the Rail Trail
cards.subtitle: New Paltz section of the Wallkill Valley Rail Trail
cards.notes: Meet at the Main Street crossing for a flat walk, jog, or bike ride. Stay right, use caution at crossings, and carry out any trash.
cards.short_summary: A year-round, free public multi-use trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wallkill Valley Land Trust says the Rail Trail is free of charge for public use from dawn to dusk, year-round.
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to dusk, year-round; its surface is unpaved stone.

cards.title: Set out on River-to-Ridge
cards.subtitle: Trailhead near 41 Springtown Road, New Paltz
cards.notes: Start with the lower, flatter section and turn around whenever the group is ready. Wear suitable footwear and bring water for this unpaved outing.
cards.short_summary: A free trail route from the village toward the ridge.
cards.evidence_claim: A Town of New Paltz trail document states that the River-to-Ridge Trail would be free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: River to Ridge Trail permit application
cards.access_notes: SUNY New Paltz advises proper footwear, caution, and letting someone know your route.

cards.title: Use the Field of Dreams exercise trail
cards.subtitle: Field of Dreams Park, New Paltz
cards.notes: Walk the exercise trail or meet by the gazebo; use the pavilion only if it is not reserved, and leave organized field use to permitted groups.
cards.short_summary: A town park with an exercise trail and open green space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of New Paltz lists an exercise trail and gazebo at Field of Dreams Park, and its park-fee policy says facilities are free to use by the public unless reserved.
cards.source_title: Town of New Paltz Parks and Pool
cards.access_notes: Pavilion use is first-come, first-served when it is not booked; do not use reserved facilities.

cards.title: Meet up at Hasbrouck Park
cards.subtitle: Tricor and Hasbrouck Avenues, New Paltz
cards.notes: Bring your own ball or simply use the gazebo and park seating. Share the basketball and pickleball courts with other users.
cards.short_summary: A village park with courts, a gazebo, and a playground.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of New Paltz lists Hasbrouck Park’s basketball courts, pickleball courts, gazebo, and playground; its park-fee policy says facilities are free to use by the public unless reserved.
cards.source_title: Town of New Paltz Parks and Pool
cards.access_notes: Located at the southwest corner of Tricor and Hasbrouck avenues; informal use only.
